draft.title: Steel or glass: which water bottle suits how you drink
draft.metaDescription: Steel against glass, decided on weight, care and where the bottle will live.
draft.intro: Glass if the bottle lives on a desk and taste matters; steel if it goes in a bag. The Clear 500 is glass and weighs 410 g for 500 ml, while the Summit Steel carries 750 ml for 340 g — glass costs you weight and capacity at the same time.

sections.heading: Weight against capacity
sections.body: The Summit Steel holds 750 ml at 340 g. The Clear 500 holds 500 ml at 410 g. That is the whole trade in one line: for a third less water you carry a fifth more bottle. On a desk it does not matter; in a rucksack it is the deciding number.

sections.heading: Care, which is where glass loses people
sections.body: The Summit Steel is hand wash only, and the Clear 500 is dishwasher safe on the top rack. If a bottle that cannot go in the dishwasher will simply not get washed, that settles it regardless of everything above.

sections.heading: The third option
sections.body: The Trail Light is tritan copolyester at 120 g for the same 750 ml as the steel, and it is dishwasher safe. It will not keep anything cold, which is the reason to rule it out rather than a detail.
